reviews.review:
# Critic — round 1

Verdict: **Not accepted as a demonstrated photorealism improvement.** The visual benefit is inconclusive at the supplied viewing scale; this is not a finding of material regression. The proposed key-share experiment did not establish the intended improvement in broad ABS reflections.

Primary evidence: all eight actual canvas full/detail plates in rounds 0 and 1, 960 × 622, identical paired cameras, desktop viewport half-resolution AO and mobile AO off. API captures are auxiliary and were not scored. Model: unchanged published 936-part Piplup 256416f99469. UI visibility changes are excluded from judgement.

## Fixed rubric

| Criterion /10 | Desktop previous | Desktop current | Mobile previous | Mobile current |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Material gloss | 5.0 | 5.0 | 5.0 | 5.0 |
| Illumination | 6.0 | 6.0 | 5.5 | 5.5 |
| Contact depth | 6.0 | 6.0 | 4.5 | 4.5 |
| Colour fidelity | 7.0 | 7.0 | 7.0 | 7.0 |
| Realism overall | 5.5 | 5.5 | 5.0 | 5.0 |

Anchors retained: 0 severely broken; 5 readable PBR with conspicuous rendering artifacts; 8 convincing photographed bricks with minor flaws; 10 photograph-like within the supplied geometry. Overall is independently judged. Colour fidelity is preservation/plausibility, not calibrated accuracy. Differences too small to support a half-point change receive no score increase.

## Visible evidence and physical references

The images do change. Small highlight/brightness shifts are visible around the red ball and model surfaces, but the dominant blue slopes and pale chest still read mostly diffuse. Neither profile convincingly gains the restrained surface and edge reflections needed to make the central build read as moulded ABS. No confident colour improvement or contact regression is visible.

I re-inspected Kenny Louie's four-brick photograph, credited at [AllAboutLean](https://www.allaboutlean.com/maybach/lego-bricks/), and the physical brick close-up used by [Henley](https://www.henley.ac.uk/events/greenlands-masterclass-unlock-the-lego-code-the-ultimate-guide-to-building-high-performing-teams). In Louie's image, saturated upper surfaces, darker vertical faces, narrow edge reflections and localized contact shadows work together. Henley's image shows small curved stud reflections and an edge glint on red plastic, without making the whole brick mirror-like. Both render versions lack comparable readable surface reflections on much of Piplup. The ball already carries a gloss cue in both versions. Photograph illumination, scale, wear and depth of field differ, so these are qualitative cues rather than exact targets.

Desktop retains a broad grey haze around the base, whereas mobile retains abrupt cast shadows and weak small contacts. Neither is resolved by the key-share change. Stepped head silhouette, angular rocks and absent moulded bevels/logos are immutable model/library geometry for this review, not evidence of a shading regression.

Read-only pixel comparison confirms nonidentical imagery: mean absolute 8-bit channel differences across the whole plates are 0.374 desktop full, 0.473 desktop detail, 0.214 mobile full and 0.282 mobile detail. These measurements establish change only; they do not measure realism.

## Performance

Metrics independently read from both packets: desktop CPU median 4.05 → 4.00 ms and synchronous GPU-drain median 752.90 → 731.20 ms; mobile CPU median 3.95 → 4.00 ms and GPU-drain median 570.15 → 564.90 ms. Twelve samples per profile. Calls remain 110/107; triangles remain 304197/304194; orbit shadow redraws remain zero; recorded errors are empty. Standard hash unchanged is supplied by the packet owner. SwiftShader variability prevents a speedup claim. No measured drawing-budget regression is established.

## Next lowest-cost priority

Test desktop GTAO radius **14 → 10 LDU only**, keeping intensity, samples, half resolution and all passes fixed. The clean plates make the broad base haze an explicit target: retain narrow stud/foot contact darkening while reducing spread outside the base. This is a parameter change in the existing pipeline and adds no geometry or passes. Risk: weaker contact depth without removing the haze; reject if that occurs. Mobile remains AO off and direct drawing; this experiment does not claim to repair its missing local occlusion. Keep the key share fixed during the next comparison rather than combining material and contact experiments.

# Independent photorealism audit — round 1

Verdict: REJECT as a demonstrated photorealism improvement. The visible benefit is inconclusive at the supplied 960 × 622 scale; no clear regression is established. This does not assert that the parameter change is technically invalid or demand a rollback. A changed source constant or key intensity is not visual proof.

Reviewed: frozen round-0 and round-1 full desktop/mobile plates from .impeccable/review/realistic-rounds/, plus all four supplied detail plates. Reopened the physical photographs rambling-penguin-front.jpg, callie-penguin.jpg and jay-transparent-canopy.jpg in .local/realistic-rounds/refs. Ignored DOM/UI. No product files changed; only this review written.

## Fixed rubric scores (0–10 per category)

| Criterion | Desktop before | Desktop current | Mobile before | Mobile current |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| ABS/specular plausibility | 4 | 4 | 4 | 4 |
| Seams/stud contact | 5 | 5 | 4 | 4 |
| Palette/tonal separation | 6 | 6 | 6 | 6 |
| Transparent water/ice | 3 | 3 | 3 | 3 |
| Grounding/photographic plausibility | 5 | 5 | 3 | 3 |
| Total /50 | 23 | 23 | 20 | 20 |

Scores remain anchored to the baseline rubric; subtle changes below a defensible one-point difference do not earn an increase. Black material has too little visible area for a detailed standalone finish verdict. Neither detail view is a true material macro, so fine seam and transmission judgments remain limited.

## Photo evidence and pair comparison

The Rambling Brick physical 40498 photographs show broad grey-blue reflected patches on black slopes, shaded white curvature, thin joints, and ground shadows strongest near support with softer falloff away from it.
https://ramblingbrick.com/2021/10/22/just-go-with-the-floe-40498-christmas-penguin-hands-on-review/
Both render versions retain relatively flat blue/white facets and a broad desktop grounding haze. Round 1 does not visibly localize that haze or provide convincingly clearer softbox reflection structure on crown/breast. At most there is subtle tonal redistribution, not a demonstrable material-category improvement.

Callie's household assembly photographs show room-shaped grey reflections in glossy black, a long soft highlight on the white belly, narrow seams, modest stud-base shadows and localized table contact shading.
https://calliesbricks.com/2022/10/23/lego-review-christmas-penguin-40498/
In both rounds the red sphere advertises gloss more clearly than Piplup's ABS surfaces. White plate detail is legible, but a clear comparable glossy response on the main subject is not established. Mobile still has the same hard, uniform grey cast-shadow silhouette; desktop still appears hazy around the platform. No persuasive contact gain or palette regression is visible.

Jay Ong's scratched physical transparent-yellow canopy shows tinted background visibility, stronger edge/wall color, bright rim reflections and faint broad reflections across panes.
https://jaysbrickblog.com/reviews/review-lego-10497-galaxy-explorer-2022/
Both rendered water regions remain pale cyan studded plastic with weak visible distinction between transmitted interior and reflective edges. No demonstrated transparency gain. The canopy is a different color/shape/background, so this compares qualitative material cues, not exact RGB or brightness. The Rambling Brick's opalescent cyan tiles are not clear-plastic calibration samples.

Geometry is unchanged in the apparent silhouettes: the crown's stair steps, projecting face plates and rock gaps are authored construction, not defects that a lighting constant can erase. Do not award geometry credit for a lighting-only change.

## Performance and packet evidence

Model 256416f99469, 936 parts, same browser 153.0.8010.12; full manifest cameras and look controls match across rounds. Key intensity changes from 2.4831117575 to 2.0175283030, consistent with the stated share change. The Standard capture SHA-256 is identical in all packets: cf7ff0a1e707d195becc8650b13df94e97fa51e0c445148378ec7ed49b7b82de. Document hashes differ across independently restored sessions, so they are not an identity-equality proof; common model/count, camera, Standard hash and geometry counters support the controlled comparison.

| Metric | Desktop before → current | Mobile before → current |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CPU median ms | 4.05 → 4.00 | 3.95 → 4.00 |
| GPU-drain median ms | 752.9 → 731.2 | 570.15 → 564.9 |
| Draw calls | 110 → 110 | 107 → 107 |
| Triangles | 304197 → 304197 | 304194 → 304194 |
| Orbit shadow redraws | 0 → 0 | 0 → 0 |

Twelve timing samples per profile/round; CPU and drain ranges overlap. No recorded errors. Structural workload is unchanged; timing is consistent with shared-machine SwiftShader variation. Speedup, proven zero runtime cost, and physical-phone performance are unsupported. Performance regression is not established either. Small offscreen capture timings are not substituted for the supplied live-canvas review plates.

## Next lowest-cost priority

Localize desktop contact shading with the existing GTAO pass: trial radius 8 instead of 14 LDU and denoise radius 3 instead of 6, leaving sample counts, resolution, lighting, exposure and geometry fixed. Judge whether the broad platform haze decreases while foot/stud contact remains readable. Parameter-only workload expectation still requires matched measurement. This trial does not improve AO-off mobile; retain its independent score rather than claiming cross-profile success. No additional passes, bevel geometry or sample increases proposed.

# Critic — round 2

**Verdict: reject.** Compared with the previous best round 0, desktop makes the repeated bands/stud-like pattern in the ground shadow more conspicuous without clearly eliminating its broad spread. Some local definition is crisper, but the foreground shadow reads less like a physical contact shadow. Mobile is unchanged: both full and detail PNG files are byte-identical to round 0.

Evidence is bounded to the paired full/detail actual canvas plates and matched metrics in rounds 0 and 2, at 960 × 622. The key-share restoration earns no credit by itself. API captures and source constants are not scored.

| Fixed criterion /10 | Desktop round 0 | Desktop round 2 | Mobile round 0 | Mobile round 2 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Material gloss | 5.0 | 5.0 | 5.0 | 5.0 |
| Illumination | 6.0 | 6.0 | 5.5 | 5.5 |
| Contact depth | 6.0 | 5.5 | 4.5 | 4.5 |
| Colour fidelity | 7.0 | 7.0 | 7.0 | 7.0 |
| Realism overall | 5.5 | 5.0 | 5.0 | 5.0 |

Rubric anchors and geometry allowance are unchanged. Overall is independent of the category average. Confidence is moderate at this viewing scale.

## Image evidence and physical-photo comparison

Desktop detail: inspect the ground immediately below the front/right base corner and outside the left edge near the pool. Round 0 has a broad soft haze; round 2 has more visible repeated light/dark bands within that spread. Narrower-looking local definition is not enough to compensate for this pattern on the surrounding ground. The ball remains glossy, while much of Piplup's blue slopes and pale chest still looks predominantly diffuse. No convincing gloss or colour gain is visible.

Compared again with the already collected [Kenny Louie four-brick photograph](https://www.allaboutlean.com/maybach/lego-bricks/), both desktop versions lack its combination of restrained surface/edge reflections and tight, continuous contact darkening. Round 2's more explicit patterned foreground shadow moves away from that cue. The collected [Henley close-up](https://www.henley.ac.uk/events/greenlands-masterclass-unlock-the-lego-code-the-ultimate-guide-to-building-high-performing-teams) shows curved stud reflections and a restrained red edge glint; neither raster version adds a comparable readable material cue to the main blue build. These photographs are qualitative material/contact references, not matched lighting or colour standards; no new broad research was performed.

Piplup's stair-stepped head, angular rock silhouettes and absent moulded bevels/logos remain geometry limits. Their shape is not charged to the AO experiment. The newly emphasized shadow pattern is a rendering issue; no normal or geometry diagnosis is claimed from these views.

## Performance

Matched metrics: desktop CPU median 4.05 → 4.65 ms, synchronous GPU-drain median 752.90 → 749.95 ms; mobile CPU median 3.95 → 3.80 ms, GPU-drain median 570.15 → 568.65 ms. Calls remain 110 desktop / 107 mobile; triangles 304197 / 304194; orbit shadow redraws zero; errors empty. No speedup or material GPU-cost change is established under SwiftShader variability.

## Next lowest-cost priority

The proposed tighter light-space shadow-map fit is justified **as a bounded phone experiment**, not as a proven solution. Mobile has weak narrow contacts at feet, rocks and stud bases, and it is worth testing whether better use of the existing map improves them. Retain map sizes, bias, filtering and caching; include caster floor projections and padding; compute bounds only after model edits. Inspect local contacts and receiver-edge coverage in the paired views. Reject if it merely sharpens already abrupt cast-shadow silhouettes, introduces acne, or crops shadows. It cannot create missing ambient occlusion or area-light penumbrae. Use the previous best round 0 as the starting comparison, since round 2 is rejected.

# Independent photorealism audit — round 2

Verdict: REJECT. My proposed GTAO reductions do not improve these plates. Desktop's broad haze becomes a darker, more sharply patterned detached shadow, particularly beneath/in front of the platform. Some haze is reduced, but the stronger repeated pale stud/stripe pattern and projected platform outline make grounding less photographic. Mobile is unchanged: both full and detail PNG SHA-256 values exactly match round 0.

Inspected supplied desktop/mobile detail pairs and local round-0/round-2 full desktop and current full mobile plates. Used the already collected physical photo evidence; no new broad research, servers or code edits. Only this permitted review file written.

| Fixed rubric /10 | Desktop round 0 | Desktop round 2 | Mobile round 0 | Mobile round 2 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| ABS/specular plausibility | 4 | 4 | 4 | 4 |
| Seams/stud contact | 5 | 5 | 4 | 4 |
| Palette/tonal separation | 6 | 6 | 6 | 6 |
| Transparent water/ice | 3 | 3 | 3 | 3 |
| Grounding/photographic plausibility | 5 | 4 | 3 | 3 |
| Total /50 | 23 | 22 | 20 | 20 |

Scores are visual judgments anchored to the baseline, not quantitative photorealism metrics. Fine seams and the small black eye areas remain difficult to assess at this scale. No new ABS, palette, transparency or geometry credit.

## Comparison with physical LEGO photographs

The Rambling Brick's studio penguin photograph has localized support shadows with softer falloff farther from contact, shaded white curves, thin seams and broad grey-blue glossy reflections on black plastic. Round 0's haze was excessive; round 2 substitutes a more legible detached patterned silhouette rather than reproducing that contact/falloff behavior.
https://ramblingbrick.com/2021/10/22/just-go-with-the-floe-40498-christmas-penguin-hands-on-review/
Local evidence: .local/realistic-rounds/refs/rambling-penguin-front.jpg.

Callie's indoor penguin photographs show restrained stud-base shadows and room-shaped plastic reflections. Shadows are naturally directional in that setting, so hardness alone is not proof of CGI. The defect here is the conspicuous uniform detached platform projection and repeated washed-out stud/stripe impressions; neither pair demonstrates better glossy response on Piplup's crown/breast. The red sphere still communicates gloss more strongly than the main ABS subject.
https://calliesbricks.com/2022/10/23/lego-review-christmas-penguin-40498/
Local evidence: .local/realistic-rounds/refs/callie-penguin.jpg and callie-build-closeup.jpg.

Jay Ong's transparent-yellow canopy has tinted background visibility, distinct edges/walls and reflection structure across its panes. Both render versions retain pale cyan water with weak transmission-versus-reflection distinction. Comparing qualitative cues only: a yellow canopy is not a blue-water calibration target. The opalescent cyan penguin-set tiles are also not a clear-plastic standard.
https://jaysbrickblog.com/reviews/review-lego-10497-galaxy-explorer-2022/
Local evidence: .local/realistic-rounds/refs/jay-transparent-canopy.jpg.

Crown steps, projecting face plates and gaps in the rock assembly remain authored geometry. Altering the AO radius does not change or repair those shapes. The packet does not isolate whether radius or denoiser adjustment caused the grounding loss, since both changed together.

## Matched metrics

Model 256416f99469, 936 parts, browser 153.0.8010.12; full cameras, look controls and 2.4831117575 key intensity match. Standard hash unchanged. Twelve timing samples per profile/round; no recorded errors.

| Metric | Desktop round 0 → round 2 | Mobile round 0 → round 2 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CPU median ms | 4.05 → 4.65 | 3.95 → 3.80 |
| GPU-drain median ms | 752.90 → 749.95 | 570.15 → 568.65 |
| Draw calls | 110 → 110 | 107 → 107 |
| Triangles | 304197 → 304197 | 304194 → 304194 |
| Orbit shadow redraws | 0 → 0 | 0 → 0 |

Structural workload unchanged. Desktop CPU median is higher, but this single noisy SwiftShader packet does not establish a performance regression. No speedup, physical-phone performance or exact zero-cost claim is supported.

## Next priority and proposed phone shadow fit

Phone grounding is a justified next target: the hard uniform grey cast silhouette is plainly visible and remains unchanged. A tighter light-space fit including caster floor projections is a reasonable resolution/coverage experiment, not an image-supported promise of better softness. These images do not establish that insufficient texel density is the dominant defect. At fixed filter/map size, tighter fitting can reduce the world-space filter footprint and sharpen shadows further; improved coverage/contact would have to outweigh that. Judge clipping, contact placement and aliasing separately from photographic falloff. Keep bounds off the orbit path and verify no new orbit redraws; fixed map size/pass count alone does not prove zero GPU or edit-time cost.

Lowest-cost directly relevant trial: restore desktop round-0 AO and try mobile shadow-ground opacity 0.3 → 0.2 only, with map, bias/filter, lighting and geometry fixed. This targets the dense grey silhouette, not its edge softness, and may weaken contact; accept only if grounding improves without a floating appearance. Prefer one variable per packet so causality is reviewable. If the shadow-fit experiment is chosen first, treat it as a resolution hypothesis with independent accept/reject criteria, not a presumed photorealism improvement.

# Critic — round 3

**Verdict: reject as a photorealism improvement.** Mobile's displaced cast-shadow silhouette is lighter, but its abrupt boundary and weak localized grounding remain. I do not see a clear new floating gap at this viewing scale, and do not claim a contact regression solely from lower opacity. The candidate nevertheless does not establish better physical grounding or material realism.

Evidence: paired round-0 and round-3 full/detail actual canvas PNGs at 960 × 622 and finalized matched metrics. No code inspection or new research was performed. Scores do not follow source constants.

| Fixed criterion /10 | Desktop before | Desktop current | Mobile before | Mobile current |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Material gloss | 5.0 | 5.0 | 5.0 | 5.0 |
| Illumination | 6.0 | 6.0 | 5.5 | 5.5 |
| Contact depth | 6.0 | 6.0 | 4.5 | 4.5 |
| Colour fidelity | 7.0 | 7.0 | 7.0 | 7.0 |
| Realism overall | 5.5 | 5.5 | 5.0 | 5.0 |

Rubric anchors and geometry allowance remain fixed. Overall is independent of the category average. Fine-detail material improvement is not awarded from these moderately distant views.

## Visible evidence and physical-photo cues

Mobile detail: the grey silhouette extending beyond the right/rear base edge becomes paler. Its outline remains equally abrupt; contact beneath the base rim does not become more legible. Feet, rocks and the ball do not gain localized contact depth. A less prominent remote silhouette is an aesthetic softening of contrast, not evidence of a softer physical shadow or stronger grounding.

Compared again against the collected [Kenny Louie brick photograph](https://www.allaboutlean.com/maybach/lego-bricks/), both mobile versions still lack its concentrated continuous darkening where objects touch their support. The collected [Henley close-up](https://www.henley.ac.uk/events/greenlands-masterclass-unlock-the-lego-code-the-ultimate-guide-to-building-high-performing-teams) also provides restrained edge and curved-stud reflection cues that neither version improves. Lighting and scale differ, so these comparisons are qualitative rather than matched targets. The candidate does not solve the relationship between the visible cast silhouette and the under-base contact.

Desktop retains the broad base haze and mostly diffuse blue surfaces. The desktop files are not byte-identical: mean absolute channel difference is 0.241 full / 0.302 detail on the 8-bit scale. Small differences occur within model regions as well; I see no consistent desktop realism change and make no attribution to the stated phone-only experiment. These pixel differences are not a realism metric.

The model's stepped head, angular rocks and absent moulded detail remain geometry limitations. Cast-shadow silhouettes legitimately reflect that geometry; their position and softness cannot be repaired by opacity alone. No geometry change is requested.

## Performance

Finalized medians: desktop CPU 4.05 → 5.05 ms, synchronous GPU-drain 752.90 → 741.10 ms; mobile CPU 3.95 → 3.50 ms, GPU-drain 570.15 → 561.90 ms. Draw calls 110/107 and triangles 304197/304194 are unchanged; orbit shadow redraws remain zero; errors empty. No speedup claim or material GPU-cost regression is supported under SwiftShader variability.

## Next priority

A single ABS roughness 0.28 → 0.22 experiment at the fixed studio is justified for testing, not adoption. Start from previous best round 0 and supply matched tight material closeups in addition to the full plates. Inspect blue curved/sloped parts, pale studs, the red ball and red rectangular bricks. Accept only if reflections become legible on the main build without pin highlights, clipped hotspots, glittering stud edges or harsher ball reflections. No new drawing pass, geometry, lighting or exposure change should accompany that test. This will not remedy missing bevels or weak ambient contact depth.

# Independent photorealism audit — round 3

Verdict: ACCEPT the phone opacity change visually as a modest grounding improvement. No new floating contact is apparent in full or detail views. This is not a physical-soft-shadow fix. Desktop equivalence remains INCONCLUSIVE: its plates are visually similar but have real decoded pixel differences, not merely PNG metadata changes. Resolve that discrepancy before claiming desktop is unchanged or giving unrestricted packet-equivalence approval.

Inspected round-0/round-3 attached desktop and mobile detail pairs, local full mobile pair and current full desktop plate. Used collected photo evidence; no new research, servers or product edits. Only this permitted review file written.

| Fixed rubric /10 | Desktop round 0 | Desktop round 3 | Mobile round 0 | Mobile round 3 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| ABS/specular plausibility | 4 | 4 | 4 | 4 |
| Seams/stud contact | 5 | 5 | 4 | 4 |

Mobile's hard grey shadow to the rear/right is lighter and less dominant. The base still reads as resting on the surface; no newly visible bright gap or loss of support is apparent. Its edge remains abrupt and its density does not become a physically varying penumbra. This earns one grounding point, not seam/contact or material points. Desktop's broad haze remains. Crown stepping, projecting face plates and rock gaps remain authored geometry. Current fine seams/black finish and transmission remain resolution-limited; no positive fine-detail inference.

## Physical-photo evidence

The Rambling Brick's studio penguin photo shows localized support shadow and softer falloff away from contact. Baseline phone had an overly heavy, uniform detached silhouette. Candidate reduces that dominance and is a modest move toward restrained grounding, while still lacking the photograph's contact-to-distance falloff. Do not call the lighter unchanged silhouette softer.

Candidate phone retains a readable supporting footprint and has no demonstrable new floating appearance. Both versions still lack comparable broad glossy reflection shapes on the main ABS subject; changing ground opacity supplies no material evidence.

Local references: .local/realistic-rounds/refs/callie-penguin.jpg and callie-build-closeup.jpg.

Jay Ong's physical transparent canopy demonstrates distinct tinted transmission, bright edges and broad reflection structure. Both packets' cyan water retain weak comparable distinction; transparency score unchanged. Different colors/backgrounds preclude direct RGB calibration, and opalescent penguin-set tiles are not clear-plastic standards.

## Packet and performance limits

Same model 256416f99469, 936 parts, browser 153.0.8010.12, full manifest camera and look controls. Standard SHA-256 remains cf7ff0a1e707d195becc8650b13df94e97fa51e0c445148378ec7ed49b7b82de. Twelve timing samples per profile/round; no recorded errors.

| Metric | Desktop round 0 → round 3 | Mobile round 0 → round 3 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CPU median ms | 4.05 → 5.05 | 3.95 → 3.50 |
| GPU-drain median ms | 752.90 → 741.10 | 570.15 → 561.90 |
| Draw calls | 110 → 110 | 107 → 107 |
| Triangles | 304197 → 304197 | 304194 → 304194 |
| Orbit shadow redraws | 0 → 0 | 0 → 0 |

Unchanged structural counters; no speedup or exact zero-runtime-cost claim. Desktop CPU increased despite intended phone-only change; a noisy packet cannot establish causality or a regression. No physical-phone performance evidence.

Desktop full/detail decoded pixels differ in 73,712 / 94,646 pixels out of 597,120, with maximum channel differences 26 / 32 (8-bit); mean absolute channel differences, including unchanged alpha, are 0.241 / 0.302. Mobile changed pixels are 3,233 / 3,868 with maximum difference 24. Pixel differences are not a photorealism metric. Desktop discrepancy may reflect capture/pipeline state, but its cause was not established. It prevents an assertion of exact desktop equivalence even though the supplied views show no clear score-level difference. No product or artifact files were modified during decoding.

## Specific next priority

Before round 4, establish why intended unchanged desktop plates differ, or obtain a reproducible matched desktop baseline. Then trial ABS roughness 0.28 → 0.22 only under the fixed studio, with matched tight closeups of blue crown slopes/studs, white breast, yellow beak/feet and red sphere, plus these whole-model views. The real photos justify testing reflection readability, not presuming lower roughness improves realism. Require coherent reflection bands following curvature and improved ABS recognition, with no isolated white stud pinpricks, lost pigment, excessively glossy sphere, seam alteration or geometry credit. Keep the accepted phone opacity fixed in both material packets and retain independent desktop/mobile scores.
